name: Profitability tree
summary: Profit = (Price × Volume) − (Fixed + Variable costs). Split the decline into revenue vs cost, then drill to the driver that moved, and always check whether the problem is company-specific or industry-wide.
opening_line: Profits fell, so I'd first check whether this is a revenue or a cost problem, and whether competitors are seeing the same thing. Then I'd drill into the specific driver that moved.
when_to_use: Profits, margins or ROI have declined or missed a target
Client asks 'how do we improve profitability?'
Post-merger results miss expectations (combine with M&A synergies)
when_not_to_use: The question is whether to enter / launch / acquire. Profitability is one branch there, not the whole structure
Pure revenue growth with no margin problem: use the growth framework
Non-profits and public sector, where the objective isn't profit

children.label: Revenue mix by product / segment / channel

buckets.name: Revenue
questions: Did price, volume or mix change?
Which products, segments, channels or regions drove it?
Is the market shrinking, or are we losing share?

buckets.name: Costs
questions: Which cost lines grew faster than revenue?
Fixed or variable? Per-unit or total?
Is it input prices, efficiency, or scale?
data_to_ask: Cost breakdown by line item over time

buckets.name: External context
questions: New entrants, substitutes, customer preference shifts?

industry_adaptations.note: Revenue = ASMs × load factor × yield (+ ancillaries). Costs are CASM: fuel, labour, aircraft ownership. Fixed-cost heavy, so load factor drives profit.
Revenue = customers × ARPU (ARR). Watch churn / net revenue retention and CAC vs LTV. COGS is hosting and support; the big costs are S&M and R&D.
Revenue = stores × traffic × conversion × basket size (+ e-com). Watch same-store sales vs new stores, gross margin (mix, shrink, markdowns) and rent / labour per sq ft.
Revenue = covers (or tickets) × average check × days. Prime cost = food + labour, usually ~60% of sales. Watch table turns and delivery-platform commissions.
Revenue = volume × reimbursement by payer mix (commercial vs Medicare / Medicaid). Watch length of stay, bed occupancy and labour (nursing) costs.
Revenue = net interest income (balances × NIM) + fees. Costs = opex (efficiency ratio) + credit losses (provisions).
Revenue = units × price. Costs: materials, direct labour, overhead absorbed by utilisation. Low capacity utilisation inflates unit cost.
Revenue = subscribers × ARPU. Watch churn, acquisition cost and network capex / depreciation (largely fixed).

common_mistakes: Listing revenue and costs generically without asking what actually changed
Forgetting the external check: is the whole industry down?
Not segmenting (products, customers, channels), so the culprit hides in an average
Jumping to cost-cutting ideas before diagnosing the cause
